summary.name: R for Data Science
summary.one_liner: Free online book (first edition website) teaching data science workflows in R: importing, tidying, transforming, visualising and modelling data.
use_cases: making plots and visualisations in R
exploring and modelling data in R
summary.what_it_does: The page is the website for the first edition of the book R for Data Science, published January 2017. It covers getting data into R, restructuring it into useful forms, transforming it, visualising it and modelling it. The book presents best practices for these tasks in R, including the grammar of graphics, literate programming and reproducible research. It also covers managing cognitive resources while wrangling, visualising and exploring data. The site lists a contributor acknowledgements section and notes it is hosted by Netlify.
notable: Website for the first edition, free to read online under CC BY-NC-ND 3.0
Written by Hadley Wickham and Garrett Grolemund (named in listing)
Physical copy can be ordered from Amazon
Covers the grammar of graphics and reproducible research workflows
caveats: This is the first edition website; the page does not say whether it is updated.
